--- name: vps-hybrid-networking description: Configure and manage a dual-layer VPS server architecture on a NAT/firewalled host (inbound ports 80/443 blocked) using Tailscale for private mesh networking and Cloudflare Tunnel + Caddy (with Cloudflare DNS-01 TLS) for high-performance public ingress. --- # VPS Hybrid Networking: Tailscale Private & Cloudflare Tunnel + Caddy Public This skill provides comprehensive setup, configuration, and troubleshooting procedures for a VPS server hosted behind a NAT/CGNAT or firewall where standard inbound ports (`80` & `443`) are blocked by the upstream provider. This architecture establishes a dual-layer network topology: 1. **Public Ingress**: Securely accessed by the public via Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`), which routes traffic to a local Caddy reverse proxy equipped with Let's Encrypt certificates issued via DNS-01 challenge. 2. **Private Network**: Server administration, internal tools (admin dashboards, terminal agents, local AI models) are served strictly over Tailscale (WireGuard mesh) without exposing any ports to the public internet. --- ## Network Architecture & Traffic Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Internet_Public["Public Internet"] Client["Public Web Client / Browser"] end subgraph Tailnet_Private["Private Network (Tailscale Mesh)"] Admin["Admin / Authorized Device"] end subgraph Cloudflare_Edge["Cloudflare Global Anycast Edge"] CF_WAF["Cloudflare Edge (DDoS, WAF, Edge SSL)"] CF_Tunnel_Edge["Cloudflare Tunnel Edge Point"] end subgraph VPS["VPS Host (Internal NAT) — Inbound Ports 80/443 BLOCKED"] direction TB Cloudflared["cloudflared daemon (Outbound QUIC/HTTP2 Tunnel)"] Tailscaled["tailscale daemon (WireGuard: 100.64.0.1)"] subgraph Caddy_Proxy["Caddy Web Server (v2 + dns.providers.cloudflare)"] SNI_Match{"SNI Match: example.com?"} VHost_Public["Virtual Host Public (example.com:443)
Cert: Let's Encrypt (DNS-01 Challenge)"] VHost_Private["Virtual Host Private (100.64.0.1:80 / ts.net)
Admin / AI / Internal Services"] end StaticFiles["/var/www/my-app
(SPA Web App & Assets)"] InternalServices["Local Services (Internal Tools / APIs)"] end Client -->|HTTPS :443| CF_WAF CF_WAF --> CF_Tunnel_Edge CF_Tunnel_Edge <===>|Outbound Persistent Tunnel| Cloudflared Cloudflared -->|"https://127.0.0.1:443 (SNI: example.com)"| SNI_Match SNI_Match -->|Valid SNI| VHost_Public VHost_Public --> StaticFiles Admin <===>|WireGuard Encrypted Mesh| Tailscaled Tailscaled --> VHost_Private VHost_Private --> StaticFiles VHost_Private --> InternalServices ``` --- ## Security Note: Is `127.0.0.1:443` Safe? **Yes, routing through `127.0.0.1:443` is an industry best practice:** - **Loopback Isolation**: `127.0.0.1` is the IPv4 loopback interface (RFC 1122). It can only be communicated with from within the local operating system kernel. It cannot be routed across the internet or reached by external actors. - **End-to-End Local Encryption**: Using `HTTPS` to `127.0.0.1:443` ensures traffic between the `cloudflared` tunnel connector and Caddy is TLS-encrypted, mitigating unencrypted snooping by other local system processes. - **Zero Inbound Exposure**: It allows you to bind services solely to loopback and VPN interfaces without opening external ports in firewalls or routers. --- ## Prerequisites & Credentials Matrix | Component | Provider / Service | Required Access | |---|---|---| | Primary Domain | Domain Registrar / Cloudflare | Nameservers delegated to Cloudflare (`*.ns.cloudflare.com`) | | Cloudflare DNS Token | Cloudflare Dashboard | Token with permission: `Zone.DNS:Edit` for the target zone | | Cloudflare Zero Trust | Cloudflare One (Zero Trust) | Free or Standard Zero Trust plan to establish Tunnels | | Tailscale Account | Tailscale Admin Console | Personal or Organization account (SSO) | | VPS Host | Linux (Debian / Ubuntu 22.04+) | `sudo` / `root` administrative privileges | --- ## Manual User Actions Checklist (Web Console Steps) The following procedures require manual interaction in the web browser and cannot be automated headlessly without interactive login: ### 1. Cloudflare Dashboard (DNS & API Token) - [ ] **Delegate Nameservers**: Ensure your domain (e.g., `example.com`) is *Active* in your Cloudflare dashboard. - [ ] **Create Cloudflare API Token for Caddy DNS-01**: 1. Navigate to [Cloudflare API Tokens](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens). 2. Click **Create Token** → select the **Edit zone DNS** template. 3. Token Name: `Caddy DNS-01 Challenge Token`. 4. Permissions: `Zone` → `DNS` → `Edit`. 5. Zone Resources: `Include` → `Specific zone` → select your domain (`example.com`). 6. Click **Continue to summary** → **Create Token**. 7. **COPY AND SAVE THIS TOKEN** (it will only be displayed once). ### 2. Cloudflare Zero Trust (Tunnel & Origin TLS Setup) - [ ] **Create Cloudflare Tunnel**: 1. Open [Cloudflare Zero Trust Dashboard](https://one.dash.cloudflare.com/). 2. Navigate to **Networks** → **Tunnels** → click **Add a tunnel**. 3. Choose **Cloudflared** → name the tunnel (e.g., `my-vps-tunnel`). 4. Copy the installation token string (or extract the token value from `--token `). - [ ] **Configure Public Hostname & CRITICAL TLS Settings**: 1. Under the **Public Hostnames** tab of your tunnel, click **Add a public hostname**. 2. Specify Hostname: - Subdomain: *(leave blank for apex, or enter `www`)* - Domain: `example.com` 3. Service: - Type: `HTTPS` - URL: `127.0.0.1:443` 4. **CRITICAL STEP (PREVENTS ERROR 525 & TLS INTERNAL HANDSHAKE ERROR)**: - Expand **Additional application settings** → select the **TLS** tab. - In the **Origin Server Name** field, enter your public domain: ``` example.com ``` *(Without this setting, `cloudflared` contacts `127.0.0.1` without SNI. Caddy cannot determine which certificate to present and rejects the TLS handshake with `remote error: tls: internal error`).* 5. Click **Save hostname**. ### 3. Tailscale Admin Console - [ ] **Authenticate Machine**: 1. Run `sudo tailscale up` on the server and complete the browser authentication link. - [ ] **Machine Settings**: 1. Set the machine name to your desired hostname (e.g., `my-vps`). 2. (Recommended) **Disable Key Expiry**: In the machine options (`...`), click **Disable key expiry** so the server connection does not expire after 180 days. 3. Ensure **MagicDNS** is enabled under the **DNS** settings tab (`*.ts.net`). --- ## Step-by-Step Server Setup Guide ### Stage 1: Verify Host Network & Inbound Port Blocking Verify whether the VPS is behind NAT and confirm inbound port blocking: ```bash # 1. Inspect local network interface and routing table ip addr show ip route show # 2. Test if external inbound traffic can reach port 80 sudo python3 -m http.server 80 & # From an external computer: curl -I http:// --connect-timeout 5 # If the request times out, inbound ports 80/443 are confirmed blocked upstream. sudo killall python3 ``` --- ### Stage 2: Private Network Setup via Tailscale ```bash # 1. Install Tailscale from its official apt repository (no pipe-to-shell installer). # Replace with ubuntu or debian and with your # release codename (e.g. noble for Ubuntu 24.04, bookworm for Debian 12). curl -fsSL https://pkgs.tailscale.com/stable//.noarmor.gpg | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/tailscale-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null curl -fsSL https://pkgs.tailscale.com/stable//.tailscale-keyring.list | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/tailscale.list sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tailscale # 2. Connect machine to your Tailnet sudo tailscale up --hostname=my-vps --accept-routes # 3. Retrieve assigned Tailscale IPv4 address (100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT range) tailscale ip -4 # Example output: 100.64.0.1 # 4. Check Tailnet node status tailscale status ``` --- ### Stage 3: Install Caddy with Cloudflare DNS-01 Plugin Standard distribution packages lack the Cloudflare DNS plugin. Download or build Caddy with `github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare`. ```bash # Download official custom Caddy binary with Cloudflare DNS plugin curl -o /tmp/caddy "https://caddyserver.com/api/download?os=linux&arch=amd64&p=github.com%2Fcaddy-dns%2Fcloudflare" chmod +x /tmp/caddy sudo mv /tmp/caddy /usr/bin/caddy # Verify the plugin is installed /usr/bin/caddy list-modules | grep dns.providers.cloudflare ``` --- ### Stage 4: Multi-Tier Caddyfile Configuration (Public & Private) Create or update `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`: ```caddy { debug } # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- # PRIVATE ENDPOINTS (Accessible Only via Tailscale Mesh Network) # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Internal Admin Terminal / Tool (e.g., ttyd) agent.example.com { tls { dns cloudflare resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 } basic_auth /* { admin } reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:7681 } # Internal AI / LLM API Gateway ai.example.com { tls { dns cloudflare resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 } reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 } # Dedicated Tailscale IP Endpoint (Accessible strictly via Tailscale IP) http://100.64.0.1 { root * /var/www/my-app encode gzip zstd file_server try_files {path} /index.html } # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- # PUBLIC ENDPOINTS (Served via Cloudflare Tunnel) # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- example.com, www.example.com { tls { dns cloudflare resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 } # Redirect Canonical WWW -> Apex @www host www.example.com redir @www https://example.com{uri} permanent # API Catalog & Metadata Headers (Optional) @api_catalog path /.well-known/api-catalog header @api_catalog Content-Type application/linkset+json @api_health path /api/v1/health header @api_health Content-Type application/json # Content Negotiation for AI / LLM Agents (Optional) @markdown { header Accept *text/markdown* not path *.webp *.svg *.jpg *.png *.css *.js *.json *.xml } rewrite @markdown /index.md header @markdown Content-Type "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" header @markdown Vary "Accept" # Static Web Application Routing root * /var/www/my-app encode gzip zstd file_server try_files {path} /index.html } ``` Format, validate, and reload Caddy: ```bash sudo caddy fmt --overwrite /etc/caddy/Caddyfile sudo caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile sudo systemctl restart caddy ``` --- ### Stage 5: Configure Cloudflare Tunnel Daemon (`cloudflared`) ```bash # 1. Install cloudflared package curl -fsSL https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-main.gpg | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg >/dev/null echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg] https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflared noble main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cloudflared.list sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y cloudflared # 2. Store the tunnel token in a protected file sudo mkdir -p /etc/cloudflared sudo tee /etc/cloudflared/token > /dev/null <<'EOF' EOF sudo chmod 600 /etc/cloudflared/token # 3. Create Systemd Service File: /etc/systemd/system/cloudflared.service sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/cloudflared.service > /dev/null <<'EOF' [Unit] Description=Cloudflare Tunnel client After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] TimeoutStartSec=15 Type=notify ExecStart=/usr/bin/cloudflared --no-autoupdate tunnel run --token-file /etc/cloudflared/token Restart=on-failure RestartSec=5s [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target EOF # 4. Reload systemd and start the tunnel daemon sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now cloudflared sudo systemctl status cloudflared ``` --- ## Smoke Testing & Verification ### 1. Test Public End-to-End Ingress (Cloudflare Edge -> Tunnel -> Caddy) ```bash curl -IL https://example.com ``` Expected output: - `HTTP/2 200 OK` - `server: cloudflare` - `content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8` ### 2. Test Content Negotiation (Markdown for Agents) ```bash curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://example.com/ ``` Expected output: - `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8` ### 3. Test Private Tailscale Ingress From an authorized device within the same Tailnet: ```bash curl -I http://100.64.0.1 ``` Expected output: - `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` - `server: Caddy` --- ## Troubleshooting Guide & Runbook ### Issue 1: Cloudflare Error 525 (SSL Handshake Failed) / `remote error: tls: internal error` * **Symptoms**: Browser displays Cloudflare Error 525. Caddy logs (`journalctl -u caddy -n 50`) show: ``` http: TLS handshake error from 127.0.0.1:...: remote error: tls: internal error ``` * **Root Cause**: `cloudflared` forwards requests to `https://127.0.0.1:443`. By default, `cloudflared` sends the loopback IP or empty SNI. Caddy has certificates for `example.com`, but no certificate exists for `127.0.0.1`, causing Caddy to reject the TLS handshake. * **Resolution**: 1. Open **Cloudflare Zero Trust** → **Networks** → **Tunnels**. 2. Edit your active tunnel → open the **Public Hostnames** tab → edit `example.com`. 3. Expand **Additional application settings** → select **TLS**. 4. In **Origin Server Name**, enter your domain name: ``` example.com ``` 5. Save the configuration. `cloudflared` will automatically reload without requiring a service restart. --- ### Issue 2: Let's Encrypt DNS-01 Challenge Failure or Timeout * **Symptoms**: Caddy log reports: ``` [ERROR] [example.com] error presenting token: ... status code 403: unauthorized / Invalid request headers ``` * **Root Causes**: 1. The Cloudflare API Token lacks `Zone.DNS:Edit` permissions. 2. The token is restricted to an incorrect zone. 3. DNS propagation delay during TXT record validation. * **Resolution**: 1. Ensure the token was created under **User API Tokens** (not the Global API Key). 2. Confirm permissions include `Zone: DNS: Edit`. 3. Specify upstream Cloudflare resolvers in the `tls` block so Caddy validates TXT records against authoritative nameservers directly: ```caddy resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 ``` --- ### Issue 3: `cloudflared.service` Crash / Restart Loop * **Symptoms**: `systemctl status cloudflared` indicates `activating (auto-restart)` or failure exit codes. * **Diagnostics**: ```bash journalctl -u cloudflared -e --no-pager ``` * **Resolution**: 1. Check if `/etc/cloudflared/token` is empty or contains unwanted trailing whitespaces. 2. Verify file permissions: Ensure `/etc/cloudflared/token` is readable (`chmod 600 /etc/cloudflared/token`). 3. Verify outbound internet connectivity to Cloudflare Edge ports (UDP/TCP `7844` or `443`): ```bash curl -v https://region1.v2.argotunnel.com ``` --- ### Issue 4: Tailscale Connectivity Interruption * **Diagnostics**: ```bash sudo tailscale status sudo tailscale ping ``` * **Resolution**: 1. If status indicates `NeedsLogin`, re-run `sudo tailscale up`. 2. If the node key expired, open the Tailscale Admin Console and select **Disable key expiry**. 3. If blocked by a local firewall, explicitly allow traffic on the `tailscale0` interface: ```bash sudo ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any ```

# VPS Hybrid Networking — Agent Skill

An agent skill for setting up a **dual-layer VPS architecture** on a host where inbound ports `80`/`443` are blocked by the provider (NAT / CGNAT / upstream firewall) — the situation you get with many budget VPS plans.

Instead of fighting the NAT, the architecture splits traffic into two layers:

- **Public ingress** — Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`) carries public traffic over an outbound connection to a local **Caddy** reverse proxy, which serves real Let's Encrypt certificates obtained via the **DNS-01 challenge** (no inbound port needed).
- **Private access** — admin tools, internal dashboards, terminal agents, and local AI services are exposed **only** over a **Tailscale** (WireGuard) mesh. Nothing internal touches the public internet.

This is not a theoretical design: it is the exact architecture running [anlian.web.id](https://anlian.web.id) in production, written up after the NAT diagnosis that led to it.

## Installation

The skill lives in [`skills/vps-hybrid-networking/`](skills/vps-hybrid-networking/) and this repo is packaged for the major agentic CLIs. Pick your tool:

### Any CLI — the universal installer (skills.sh)

```bash
npx skills add AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking
```

The [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) auto-detects 75+ agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Hermes Agent, Windsurf, Cline, …) and installs the skill into the right folder for each. Add `-g` for a global install, or `--agent <name>` to target one agent.

### Claude Code — plugin marketplace

```
/plugin marketplace add AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking
/plugin install vps-hybrid-networking@anlian-skills
```

### Antigravity (`agy`)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking
agy plugin validate --strict ./vps-hybrid-networking
agy plugin install ./vps-hybrid-networking
```

### Codex — plugin marketplace

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking
codex plugin add vps-hybrid-networking@anlian-skills
```

### Gemini CLI

As a skill:

```bash
gemini skills install https://github.com/AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking.git --path skills/vps-hybrid-networking --consent
```

Or as an extension (bundles the same skill):

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking
```

### Hermes Agent (Nous Research)

Hermes installs skills straight from GitHub — the identifier is the repo-relative path to the skill folder:

```bash
hermes skills install AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking/skills/vps-hybrid-networking
```

Hermes security-scans skills on install. You can also register this repo as a reusable source once with `hermes skills tap add AnandaAp/vps-hybrid-networking`.

> **Note on the Hermes security scan:** this skill is a root-level server-administration runbook, so Hermes' pattern scanner flags its subject matter (`sudo`, systemd units, files under `/etc`, network tunnels) and hub installs are currently blocked with a "dangerous" verdict. The flagged operations are the setup itself, run on your own server with your own tokens — but review the findings before trusting any skill, including this one. If you have reviewed it and want it anyway, install manually: copy `skills/vps-hybrid-networking/` into your Hermes skills folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\skills\` on Windows, `~/.hermes/skills\` elsewhere) and restart Hermes.

### npm / npx installer (this repo's own package)

```bash
npx vps-hybrid-networking@1.0.4
```

Auto-detects your installed agents and copies the skill into each one's skills folder. Targets: Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex / agents standard, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Hermes Agent, Cline, Roo Code, Goose, Amp, Windsurf, Kiro CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot, Trae, and Continue. Useful flags: `--all`, `--agent claude-code,antigravity`, `--list`, `--dry-run`. (If the npm package is not yet published, clone this repo and run `node bin/install.mjs --all` — it is the same code with the same result.)

Runs on **Windows, macOS, and Linux**. Platform notes: on macOS and Linux, the XDG-style targets (OpenCode, Goose, Amp) honor `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when it is set — matching how those tools resolve their own config directories (OpenCode uses `~/.config/opencode` on macOS too, not `~/Library`). Hermes uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\skills\` on Windows and `~/.hermes/skills/` on macOS/Linux.

### Manual

Copy the `skills/vps-hybrid-networking/` folder into your agent's skills directory (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.gemini/config/skills/`, `~/.hermes/skills/` — on Windows, Hermes uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\skills\`). Done — the skill is just files.

## Installer security

The npm installer is built to be boring and auditable:

- **Zero dependencies** — Node.js standard library only; there is no dependency tree to compromise.
- **No install hooks** — `package.json` defines no lifecycle scripts, so nothing runs implicitly on `npm install`/`npx`. The installer runs only when you invoke it.
- **No network, no execution** — the installer never downloads anything and never spawns a process. It only copies the skill files bundled inside the package into a fixed allow-list of well-known agent folders, and it verifies every destination stays inside its allow-listed folder before copying.
- **Pin the version** (`npx vps-hybrid-networking@1.0.4`) if you want reproducible installs, and read [`bin/install.mjs`](bin/install.mjs) — it is short on purpose.
- Prefer not to run third-party installers at all? Use `npx skills add` (which pulls straight from GitHub) or the manual copy above.

## What's inside

[`skills/vps-hybrid-networking/SKILL.md`](skills/vps-hybrid-networking/SKILL.md) is a complete, self-contained runbook your agent can follow end to end:

- Architecture diagram and traffic flow (public vs. private)
- Manual web-console checklists (Cloudflare DNS + API token, Zero Trust tunnel, Tailscale admin)
- A staged server setup guide:
  1. Verifying NAT / blocked inbound ports
  2. Tailscale private network setup
  3. Installing Caddy with the Cloudflare DNS plugin
  4. A multi-tier Caddyfile (public vhosts + Tailscale-only private vhosts)
  5. Running `cloudflared` as a hardened systemd service
- Smoke tests for public ingress, markdown content negotiation, and private ingress — plus a bundled `scripts/verify-networking.sh` that checks host networking, Tailscale, Caddy, and the tunnel in four steps
- A troubleshooting runbook covering the classic failure modes — Error 525 / TLS SNI handshake failure, DNS-01 challenge errors, `cloudflared` crash loops, and Tailscale connectivity loss

## Requirements

- A domain with nameservers delegated to Cloudflare
- A Cloudflare API token with `Zone → DNS → Edit`, scoped to that zone only
- A Cloudflare Zero Trust plan (free tier works) for the tunnel
- A Tailscale account
- A Debian / Ubuntu 22.04+ VPS with `sudo`

All hostnames, IPs, and tokens in the skill are placeholders (`example.com`, `100.64.0.1`, `<YOUR_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN>`) — substitute your own values on the server.

## Security notes

- **Never commit real tokens.** This repo ships placeholders only. Keep real API tokens and tunnel tokens in protected files on the server (e.g. `/etc/cloudflared/token`, mode `600`), or reference them in the Caddyfile via `{env.CF_API_TOKEN}` instead of hardcoding the value.
- Scope the Cloudflare token to a single zone with DNS Edit only — it cannot touch your account or other domains.
- The `.gitignore` in this repo excludes `.env` files, token files, certificates, and real `Caddyfile`s, so your working configs can't slip into a commit by accident.
